lenses.concrete_proposal:
## J-space integration for HLWM v10 (prep on Mac, use on 2xT4; prereg gets an amended section, no silent edits)

### Phase 0 — Build the J-dictionary on the pinned FROZEN Qwen3-0.6B (Mac, ~1-2h wall; new script scripts/build_j_dictionary.py; new module bundle/hlwm_kaggle/j_lens.py)
Key cost collapse: we do not need the full J_l (d x d per layer; the paper's pseudocode does one backward per output DIMENSION, A.7). We only need J-lens vectors v_t(l) = row t of W_U J_l for a curated token set T. Row t of W_U J_l = grad wrt h_{l,pos} of sum_{t'} (u_t . z_{t'}) — so ONE backward per (token, prompt-batch) yields the row at ALL layers and ALL source positions simultaneously (autodiff causality gives t'>=t for free; this is exactly the paper's pseudocode loss with e_i replaced by u_t, i.e., composing with the unembedding before the backward).

Recipe (each choice cites the paper's measured ablation):
1. Corpus: 256 sequences x 128 tokens from a pretraining-like distribution (wikitext-103 slice, tokenized with the pinned tokenizer). Paper default is 1000x128 but Figs 59-60 show the J-lens beats logit/tuned lens at 10 prompts with only modest gains beyond; 256 is a 4x safety margin over the knee.
2. Token set T (~200, every entry ASSERTED single-token under the pinned Qwen3 tokenizer in a blocking CPU preflight): digits "0".."9" bare + space-prefixed (20); number words zero..twenty + tens, space-prefixed, keeping only single-token ones (~25); operator words (plus, minus, times, sum, total, product, add, subtract, divide, half, twice) (~20); symbols + - * / = % (~6); unit/domain words from our anchor families (hours, dollars, meters, percent, remainder, count, left, each, per) (~25); decision tokens (answer, equals, result, yes, no, none, unknown, uncertain, abst-first-token if single, sorry) (~12); family-content vocabulary auto-extracted from the anchor generator filtered to single tokens, cap 80; scaffold-hazard tokens (Human, Assistant) kept as a NEGATIVE telemetry sublist, excluded from the alignment span.
3. Gradient target: penultimate-layer residual stream (A.7: "including the last layer can sometimes increase... noisy artifacts"; default lens uses penultimate). No QK stop-grad in v1 (A.7 notes stop-grad slightly increases causal effect; recorded as a variant, not a knob).
4. Aggregation (A.7): within-prompt mean over source positions, excluding the first 8 positions and positions whose residual norm exceeds within-prompt mean + 4 sigma; across prompts per-element mean with a Frobenius-norm outlier pre-filter (mean + 4 sigma).
5. Mechanics: batch 16 prompts; one forward with retain_graph; per token t in T, backward from sum over batch and positions of u_t . z_penult; harvest grads at all 28 layers via retain_grad hooks; reduce immediately to [28, 1024] running means. Total = 200 tokens x 16 chunks = 3200 backwards of a 0.6B at seq 128 (~0.5-1s each on M-series => ~1-1.5h; ~15 min if done on T4 instead).
6. Band selection (paper Fig 28 metrics, cheap because lens application is a matmul): on 32 held-out prompts compute per-layer excess kurtosis of readout logits and top-k agreement with the model's actual next token; pick the contiguous band where kurtosis is high and top-k agreement has NOT yet spiked (paper: ~38%-92% of depth on Sonnet => prior of layers 10-25 of 28 for Qwen; preflight P-J5 falls back to the fixed prior with disclosure if the metrics are non-informative at 0.6B).
7. Artifacts shipped in the bundle: j_lens.npz containing V[l][t] fp16 (200 x 28 x 1024 = ~11.5 MB), per-band-layer orthonormal span basis Q_l (QR of the dictionary, rank<=200, ~6.5 MB), the token list + tokenizer ids, band indices, corpus sha. Manifest code_sha256 covers it; the notebook verifies BEFORE training (v6.0 stale-sha lesson).

### (a) Aligning KV-slot VALUE writes with J-space (modeling_hlwm.py + train_kaggle.py)
The J-space lives in residual-stream coordinates; the slots live in K/V space. The residual-stream write of slot s at layer l is (to first order, uniform-read approximation mirroring the paper's own MLP-gain caveat, S4.3.1 fn 5): w_{s,l} = o_proj_l(repeat_interleave(V_slot[s], gqa_groups)). Implementation:
- New method KVPrefixProjector.slot_residual_writes(kv_slots, o_proj_weights) computing w_{s,l} for band layers only (frozen o_proj weights are already resident; one 1024x1024 matmul per band layer per step, negligible vs 13-17s steps).
- New auxiliary loss in v10_training_step: L_jalign = mean over band layers l, slots s of ||w - Q_l Q_l^T w||^2 / (||w||^2 + eps), weight config.j_align_weight = 0.05. Direction-only (ratio form) so it cannot be satisfied by shrinking V (magnitude is owned by the existing producer losses); LINEAR span projection at train time (the sparse nonneg CONE of A.8 is reserved for telemetry/audit; deviation from the paper's cone definition disclosed in the prereg amendment — a 200-token span of rank<=200 in d=1024 is still selective). KEYS are left free: A.7's frozen-QK analysis separates "what gets moved" (values — this is what we align) from "what gets attended" (keys — the gates' job). Gradient is structurally live at init because slot projections are small-normal (never zero) and w is generically not in the span; certified by preflight, not by argument.
- ALTERNATIVE hard arm (audit only, no training change): inference hooks that replace w by Q Q^T w (J-project) or w - Q Q^T w (J-perp) on band layers. This transplants the paper's Fig 8 experiment onto our channel: the paper predicts the J-projected arm retains most of the generation effect and the perp arm kills it. Run J-perp on a 64-row audit subset (one extra decode pass) as the mechanism-attribution arm.

### (b) Verbalizability probe upgrade (evaluate_v10.py, train_premise_probe)
Keep the existing free linear probe (it measures "information present"). Add, on the SAME held-out rows and the same cached band-layer hidden states at the pre-answer position (already hooked for the all-layer smoothL1 distillation):
- J-coordinate features per the paper's probe form (S2.5: "we read the score (or cosine similarity) of h against a single chosen v_t"): x = concat over 3 designated band layers of cos(h_l, v_t(l)) for t in T (~600 dims), fed to the same regularized logistic as today; and a zero-parameter argmax read over the 20 digit-token scores (strictest "verbalizable" decode).
- Report the triple (free acc, J-logistic acc, J-argmax acc). New DECIDABLE diagnostic gate J2 (first run diagnostic, not pass-blocking): if free-probe >= chance+0.10 AND J-argmax < chance+0.05, the audit names the outcome "non-verbalizable channel" — the ten-study signature reproduced with its paper-grounded mechanism (Fig 8: non-J component = decodable variance, ~0 report), instead of another unexplained 0.000.

### (c) J-occupancy telemetry (train_kaggle.py, every 256 steps on a fixed 32-row diag batch)
At band-start/mid/end layers: nonnegative gradient-pursuit decomposition (k = 1..12) of pre-answer residual states over the 200-vector dictionary vs a fixed 200-random-unit-direction control (paper S4.2 definition): log occupancy (first k where marginal reconstruction gain drops below control), excess variance explained at k=8, plus slot-write J-fraction ||Q Q^T w||^2/||w||^2, plus scaffold-token (Human/Assistant) J-scores as a leak canary. Expectation written into the prereg: J-fraction rises above its step-0 value; paper calibration says do NOT expect dominance (excess variance never exceeded 10% even on Sonnet). Cost: 200-dim least squares on ~100 vectors, <5s per invocation.

### Blocking CPU preflights (all in v10_preflight, tiny-config runnable)
P-J1 every token in T is exactly one token id; dictionary has no NaN/inf, per-layer matrix rank equals |T| up to tolerance. P-J2 finite-difference gradient-liveness of L_jalign at init on random slots + random dictionary (asserts nonzero grad through V-path; kills the v8 scale-invariance/inert-gradient class). P-J3 gradient pursuit recovers a planted 5-sparse nonneg combination and scores random noise at control level. P-J4 j_lens.npz sha verified against manifest before any GPU commitment. P-J5 band metrics computed on shipped mini-corpus produce a contiguous band, else fixed fallback layers 10-25 with a disclosure flag in metrics. Plus unit tests: J-project + J-perp hooks sum to identity; analytic J-lens check on a linear toy model (J_l equals the product of downstream linear maps exactly).

### Budget
Prep: Mac ~1-2h (or 15 min T4 pre-train cell). Bundle +~20 MB. Train: +1 matmul chain per band layer per step (<0.3s, <2.5% of step). Telemetry: <5s per 256 steps. Audit: +1 decode pass (J-perp arm, 64 rows) + probe features from already-cached states. Fits the 12h session with the existing 2000-step plan untouched. Optional post-train J refresh on T4 (100 tokens x 64 prompts, ~5 min) as a robustness row, frozen-base dictionary remains canonical since the frozen lm_head is what the per-latent decode CE already targets.

### Prereg
Amended section "S12 J-space instrumentation (arXiv:2607.15495)" appended to reports/hlwm-v10-plan-2026-09-03.md: J1 alignment loss (weight 0.05, band-only, ratio form, linear-span deviation disclosed), J2 verbalizability probe + decidable non-verbalizable-channel naming rule, J3 telemetry + expectations, the five preflights, and the J-perp audit arm with its paper-predicted direction of effect.

findings.claim: The J-lens is a per-layer averaged Jacobian J_l = E_{t, t'>=t, prompt}[dh_final,t' / dh_l,t], read out as lens(h) = softmax(W_U norm(J_l h)); the J-lens vectors are the rows of W_U J_l, one residual-stream direction per vocabulary token.
findings.paper_evidence: S2.1: "we compute J_l = E_{t, t'>=t, prompt}[dh_final,t'/dh_l,t] ... a corpus of one thousand prompts ... lens(h_l) = softmax(W_U norm(J_l h_l))"; "We refer to the rows of W_U J_l as the Jacobian lens (J-lens) vectors at layer l". Pseudocode in A.7 confirms: sum over target positions t', mean over source positions t, per-element mean over prompts.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Because we only need ~200 curated rows of W_U J_l (not the full d x d matrix), each row is one backward pass from u_t . z summed over positions, harvesting all 28 layers at once — the extraction cost collapses from d_model=1024 backwards/prompt to |T|~200 backwards/prompt-batch, making a faithful J-dictionary buildable on a Mac in ~1-2h for the pinned frozen Qwen3-0.6B.

findings.claim: A tiny corpus suffices: the J-lens beats logit-lens and tuned-lens baselines with as few as 10 prompts, with only modest improvement up to the default 1000 sequences of 128 tokens.
findings.paper_evidence: A.7 Data: "Our default lens uses one thousand sequences of 128 tokens each. We sweep the number of prompts from 1 to 1000 ... J-lens beats the logit lens and tuned lens baselines with as few as 10 prompts, with modest improvements coming from additional data" (Figs 59-60). Distribution restrictions and position masking "yielded no meaningful improvement".
findings.hlwm_relevance: 256 wikitext sequences x 128 tokens is a 25x margin over the measured knee — the whole dictionary build fits prep-budget, and an in-session T4 refresh (64 prompts) is a ~5-minute optional robustness row.

findings.claim: Measured recipe ablations: taking the gradient target at the PENULTIMATE layer reduces noisy artifacts, QK stop-grad increases causal effect, and mean aggregation with outlier-position exclusion is the best default; results are otherwise robust across the 5 recipe variants tested.
findings.paper_evidence: A.7 Gradient of What?: "including the last layer can sometimes increase the number of noisy artifacts"; "mean aggregation of penultimate is a small improvement in extracting intermediates, and applying stop-grads to QK can increase the causal effect" (Figs 57-58); within-prompt exclusion of first positions and norm outliers (N sigma).
findings.hlwm_relevance: Fixes every free choice in our build script by citation instead of taste: penultimate target, full-gradient (stop-grad recorded as variant), skip first 8 positions, 4-sigma norm filters — no untested knobs enter the prereg amendment.

findings.claim: The J-space is formally the union of k-sparse nonnegative cones over the J-lens vectors (k ~ 25); membership is operationalized by gradient pursuit, and the J-space component of x is the nearest-cone projection Pi_S x with distance d_F(x) = min_{|S|=k} ||x - Pi_S x||.
findings.paper_evidence: S2.3: "we define the J-space as the set of points expressible as a sparse nonnegative combination of J-lens vectors ... typically choose it to be no more than 25"; A.8: "F = union_{|S|=k} span{v_i} ... d_F(x) := min_{|S|=k} ||x - Pi_S x||", with gradient pursuit [116,19] as the solver (S2.5).
findings.hlwm_relevance: Gives the exact math for our occupancy telemetry and audit-time projection arms; we disclose one deviation — the training loss uses the linear span of the curated 200-token dictionary (rank<=200 in d=1024, still selective) because per-step cone projection is too expensive, while the cone/gradient-pursuit form is used verbatim for telemetry and the probe.

findings.claim: Verbalizable content is privileged and tiny: a concept's J-space component carries a median of only 6-7% of its vector variance yet drives verbal report (59% swap-to-top-5 vs 88% for pure J-lens vectors), while the ~93%-variance non-J component succeeds on only 5% of trials — and clamping J re-entry drives even that residual effect to ~zero.
findings.paper_evidence: S3.1 / Fig 8: "the J-space component carries a median of only 6-7% of the concept vector's variance, with the remaining ~93% lying outside"; "swapping along the concept vectors' J-space components drives the swap target into the model's top-5 outputs on 59% of trials ... non-J-space components succeed on only 5%"; "Under this clamp, the non-J-space component's effect falls to zero in the swap experiment".
findings.hlwm_relevance: This is a measured mechanistic model of HLWM's ten-study failure signature: a linear probe reads the 93%-variance non-J component (probe ~0.30), but generation only consumes J-space content (0.000). It converts our headline risk into a testable target — put the KV-slot writes' content INTO J-space coordinates — and predicts the direction of our J-perp audit ablation.

findings.claim: The J-space acts as a workspace only in an intermediate layer band (~38%-92% of depth on Sonnet), with the band boundaries measurable by cheap lens-derived statistics: readout excess kurtosis, top-1 autocorrelation across positions, top-k next-token agreement, and effective dimensionality.
findings.paper_evidence: S4.1 / Fig 28: "beginning about a third of the way through (~L38) and ending shortly before the output (~L92)"; final layers are a "motor" regime where readouts align with the imminent output; kurtosis "near zero through the first third", next-token accuracy "jumps steeply in the final few layers". S4.1.1: ambiguous-input interpretation snaps to bimodal exactly at the onset layer (38).
findings.hlwm_relevance: Align, probe, and inject only inside the band (prior: Qwen3-0.6B layers ~10-25 of 28), and measure the band empirically in prep with the same two cheapest metrics (kurtosis + top-k agreement) rather than assuming Sonnet's fractions transfer; preflight P-J5 covers the fallback.

findings.claim: J-space occupancy plateaus around 25 active vectors in the workspace band (defined against a same-size random-direction control), and the J-space carries at most ~10% excess activation variance — dominance is never expected even in a healthy workspace.
findings.paper_evidence: S4.2 / Fig 30: "Occupancy is near zero through the first third of the layers and rises to a plateau of around 25"; "The excess variance explained is modest, never exceeding 10%, indicating that the model's activations are dominated by information outside the J-space."
findings.hlwm_relevance: Defines our telemetry metric verbatim (occupancy vs random-control marginal gain; excess variance at k=8) AND calibrates its pass expectations: the gate is "slot-write J-fraction rises above step-0 and occupancy exceeds control", not "J-fraction near 1" — preventing us from preregistering an unwinnable threshold, the v6.0 headline mistake.

findings.claim: The frozen model's MLPs preferentially amplify J-space directions ~10x within the workspace band (vs ~1x for random and for single-neuron output directions).
findings.paper_evidence: S4.3.1 / Fig 32: "their gain sits near 1 before the workspace onset, rises through the workspace range to roughly 10x, and falls again in the final layers", gain defined as MLP output norm at layer l+1 on direction v normalized by median over isotropic random directions (with the footnote-5 first-order caveat).
findings.hlwm_relevance: The mechanistic reason KV-slot value writes aligned to J-space should actually steer generation through a FROZEN backbone: the base model's own MLPs amplify exactly those directions ~10x downstream, whereas our historical arbitrary latent directions got gain ~1 — information injected but never amplified into the decode path.

findings.claim: The J-lens supports a cheap per-token probe form — the score or cosine of h against a single J-lens vector v_t — and a sparse-decomposition inventory form, both used throughout the paper; at use time the lens is "a single precomputed matrix multiply per layer".
findings.paper_evidence: S2.5: "we read the score (or cosine similarity) of h_l against a single chosen v_t ... when measuring whether a specific concept is present above a threshold"; sparse decomposition by gradient pursuit "underlies our occupancy estimate". S8/S9: "cheap to compute (a single matrix multiplication per layer, with the matrix computed once per model), requires no auxiliary training".
findings.hlwm_relevance: The audit's premise probe upgrades verbatim: features become cos(h_l, v_t) over the 200-token dictionary at 3 band layers (plus a zero-parameter argmax over the 20 digit tokens), reusing hidden states already cached for the distillation loss — near-zero added audit compute.

findings.claim: J-lens vectors are causally load-bearing for report and reasoning: coordinate swaps redirect answers (spider->ant flips "8" to "6"), planned-rhyme swaps change earlier word choices, and injected vectors are reported on the majority of introspection trials.
findings.paper_evidence: S3.1: swap drives targets to top-5 88% (pure J-lens vectors); "The model reports the injected concept in the majority of trials" (Fig 7). S3.3 / Figs 12-13: "When we swap the spider lens vector for ant, the model's top output changes from '8' to '6'"; rhyme swap changes "coming fight" to "morning light" including earlier positions.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Justifies the two inference-time audit arms as experiments with paper-measured expected effect directions: J-project on slot writes should preserve the channel's generation effect; J-perp should kill it. A perp-arm null against a dead channel would be the first mechanism-attributed negative in the program's history rather than a bare 0.000.

findings.claim: The J-lens covers only single-token concepts; multi-token words need the separate template lens (a few hundred forward passes per word, with tuned-lens-like skip-ahead pathologies), and J-lens readout/swap performance degrades sharply with intermediate token length.
findings.paper_evidence: S9.1 limitation via A.9: "Words like 'blackmail' or 'photosynthesis' ... have no corresponding J-lens vector"; Fig 62: "the J-lens decodes single-token intermediate concepts well but degrades in performance sharply as the intermediate grows longer"; template lens "requires a few hundred forward passes per word rather than a single set of backward passes per layer".
findings.hlwm_relevance: Constrains the token-set design: every dictionary entry must be verified single-token under the pinned Qwen tokenizer (blocking preflight P-J1), our arithmetic/abstention domain is naturally single-token-rich (digits, operators, yes/no), and the template lens is explicitly out of the 1-day scope.

findings.claim: Workspace strength scales with model size, and all quantitative results are from Claude Sonnet/Haiku/Opus-class post-trained models (25 subsampled layers, reindexed 0-100), so band location, occupancy ~25, and modulation rates are not guaranteed at 0.6B — though open-source-model readouts exist (Neuronpedia).
findings.paper_evidence: S3.2 / Fig 10: target appears in the lens on a substantial fraction of trials "and this tends to increase with model size"; S2.5: "we report results on 25 evenly spaced layers ... By default, we report results on Claude Sonnet 4.5 ... Haiku 4.5 and Opus 4.5 ... Opus 4.6"; S2.2: "J-lens readouts on open-source models can be found on Neuronpedia".
findings.hlwm_relevance: Forces the honesty posture of the amendment: the verbalizability-probe gate J2 is DIAGNOSTIC on first run with a decidable failure-naming rule (free-probe high + J-argmax at chance => "non-verbalizable channel"), the band is measured on Qwen rather than copied, and a weak 0.6B J-space is itself a reportable outcome, not a silent gate failure.

lenses.lens: THE JACOBIAN LENS, EXACTLY: per-layer averaged Jacobians J_l = E[dh_final/dh_l] whose rows under W_U define one verbalizable direction per token; the k-sparse nonnegative cone hull of those directions (the J-space) is the model's global workspace — reportable, amplified 10x by frozen MLPs, privileged for generation despite carrying <10% of activation variance.
lenses.what_does_not_transfer: (1) Scale: every number is from Sonnet/Haiku/Opus-class post-trained assistants; directed modulation strength explicitly increases with model size (Fig 10), so Qwen3-0.6B's workspace band may be narrower/noisier and occupancy well below ~25 — our band and occupancy priors must be re-measured, not copied. (2) The introspection/modulation protocols ("hold X in mind", injected-thought reporting) presuppose a post-trained assistant with instruction-following depth a 0.6B fine-tune lacks; none of those results are load-bearing for our design. (3) The paper's interventions are inference-time patches on natural prompts; it contains NO experiment where a trainable module is optimized to WRITE into J-space (the closest is counterfactual reflection training, S7, which shapes the workspace indirectly via SFT) — our L_jalign is an extrapolation, which is why it ships as a 0.05-weight auxiliary plus audit-time projection arms rather than a hard constraint. (4) The J-lens is a first-order linearization averaged over a pretraining-like corpus; strong learned KV-slot writes may leave the linear regime, and our uniform-read o_proj approximation of the slot's residual write ignores per-head attention weighting (same class of caveat the paper itself flags for its MLP-gain metric, fn 5). (5) Multi-token concepts have no J-lens vector and the template/oracle lenses (hundreds of forwards per word, RL-trained oracle) are out of budget — our dictionary is single-token only, which fits arithmetic/abstention but would not transfer to SQL or free-text families. (6) Their compute idiom (full d_model x d_model J_l via one backward per output dimension over 1000 prompts) does NOT transfer and does not need to: the curated-row shortcut is faithful to the same definition at ~1/5000 of the cost, but it means we never possess the full lens and cannot rank the whole vocabulary — scaffold-leak telemetry is limited to the hazard tokens we explicitly enrolled.

lenses.lens: WORKSPACE FUNCTIONAL EXPERIMENTS AS HLWM TESTS — mapping the J-space paper's report/summon/hold/argument-passing/selectivity measurements onto v10 audit arms and gates

findings.claim: Direct injection of known content into the workspace, bypassing the model's own writer, is the paper's cleanest channel diagnostic — and it separates 'writer never wrote' from 'reader cannot read'.
findings.paper_evidence: §3.1 (The J-space supports verbal report): injecting a single J-lens vector on the user turn makes 'the model report the injected concept in the majority of trials' (Fig 7, median reciprocal rank vs steering strength, n=100 concepts); the swap experiment: 'After this swap, the model reports Rugby'; scaled version 'reliably shifts the implanted concept toward the top of the model's output distribution' (Fig 6 bottom right).
findings.hlwm_relevance: This is the exact missing arm in v10's a–h set. All current arms perturb or remove the writer's output; none writes KNOWN-GOOD content into the slots. train_kaggle.py Group C already builds `colar_thoughts = compressed_gold_thoughts(...)` and feeds them as BOTH thought_embeds and thought_states through student_channel_teacher_force — so a gold-injection decode arm is in-distribution for the reader BY TRAINING CONSTRUCTION. If gold-injected masked accuracy is high while arm_full is low, the producer failed; if gold-injected accuracy is at floor, the reader/interface is dead despite explicit odd-step training on that distribution — the sharpest possible negative, and it decides which component the next rung must fix.

findings.claim: Probe-presence of a concept does not predict causal use: information can sit in the workspace at comparable rates across tasks while being causally consumed only for report and flexible computation.
findings.paper_evidence: §3.5.1: language experiment, Fig 20 — 'the language name appears in J-lens readouts at comparable rates in all four conditions (panel b), but its causal role differs sharply' — report/flexible-inference flip under swap 'on essentially every trial, while continuation and anomaly detection are largely unmoved (panel c)'.
findings.hlwm_relevance: This is the ten-study failure signature (probe ~0.30 decodable, generation 0.000) reproduced at frontier scale and given a measurement discipline: the ONLY valid channel-liveness metrics are causal (swap/injection flip rates), never probe accuracy. v10's premise probe must stay telemetry; the preregistered channel gates should be the causal arms.

findings.claim: The causal test for content transmission is the FLIP metric — grade the swapped run against the DONOR's answer key, not merely degradation against the row's own key.
findings.paper_evidence: §3.3: two-hop coordinate swaps flip the answer to the swap target on '54% of trials on Haiku 4.5, 70% on Sonnet 4.5, and 70% on Opus 4.5' (Fig 15); probe-decomposition swap: J-space component flips 61% vs non-J 28%, falling to 6% when J-coordinates are clamped (Fig 16); bandit example flips both directions ('happy' A→B, 'sad' B→A, Fig 14).
findings.hlwm_relevance: v10's arm_shuffled already runs a within-family derangement but only measures degradation to floor — which cannot distinguish 'channel carries row-specific content' from 'channel is a family-ID/format relay' (a preregistered v9/v10 confound class). Re-grading the SAME shuffled decodes against each donor row's answer key costs zero extra GPU decodes and adds the paper's strongest positive metric: flip rate over rows where donor answer differs from own answer.

findings.claim: Intervention effects should be dose-responsive; swap success scales with intervention strength and with how strongly the source concept was loaded in the workspace.
findings.paper_evidence: §3.4: 76/192 swaps succeed at alpha=1 vs 101/192 at 'double strength' alpha=2 (Fig 19 left); 'Workspace loading of the source argument predicts swap success well' (Fig 19 right); §3.1 Fig 7 sweeps injection strength and plots median reciprocal rank against it.
findings.hlwm_relevance: A dose-response curve (interpolating pause→real or pause→gold thoughts) distinguishes a graded, live channel from a dead one (flat curve) or a brittle binary trigger, with two free bit-exact endpoint checks: lambda=0 must reproduce arm_pause and lambda=1 must reproduce arm_full — a CPU-testable correctness preflight. The loading analog is per-row cosine(ground_latents(thought_embeds), compressed_gold targets) — already the producer-MSE quantity — preregisterable as a covariate predicting per-row injectability.

findings.claim: Workspace ablation must come with a targetedness control: it should devastate flexible reasoning while leaving generic next-token prediction intact.
findings.paper_evidence: §3.5.2: heavy ablation drops multihop accuracy 'to near zero' while 'pretraining top-1 match' — agreement of ablated vs unablated top-1 over pretraining-like text — remains high (Fig 22), with a random-direction control at matched layers; Fig 24 battery: shallow tasks (MMLU, SQuAD, sentiment, CoLA) 'essentially unaffected even under heavy ablation'.
findings.hlwm_relevance: v10's arm_slot_ablation measures only anchor accuracy. Adding a top-1-match telemetry (full vs slot-ablated next-token agreement on a small neutral-text set) certifies the channel is selective: large anchor delta + high neutral agreement = a real reasoning channel; large deltas everywhere = the slots became a generic fluency crutch; no delta anywhere = dead interface.

findings.claim: Information can be 'pulled into' the workspace on demand — occupancy is task-conditional, highest when the content must be held for a further operation.
findings.paper_evidence: §3.5.1 counting task, Fig 21: number tokens 'entirely absent from the lens' under automatic linewrap, present 'at twenty positions' under explicit report, and 'at still more lens positions' under the first-letter (flexible-computation) question; §3.2: under 'think about X' the target enters the lens while a no-instruction baseline is 'approximately zero'.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Two implications: (1) our masked anchors are the flexible-computation condition — the category the paper shows DOES route through the workspace, so the task design is on the right side of the automaticity boundary; (2) a cheap 'summoning' telemetry exists: compare premise-probe accuracy on thought_states between masked rows (premise needed downstream) and unmasked rows (premise visible in the student prompt, not needed from the channel) — a live writer should load the premise harder when the decoder is starved.

findings.claim: The causally effective component can be a tiny fraction of representational variance; interventions on the bulk (non-workspace) component barely move behavior and what effect they have routes back through the workspace.
findings.paper_evidence: §3.1 Fig 8: the J-space component carries 'a median of only 6–7% of the concept vector's variance' yet drives 59% top-5 swap success vs 5% for the ~93%-variance remainder; clamping J-coordinates to clean-pass values drops the remainder's effect 'to zero'; §3.3 Fig 16: probe J-component 61% vs non-J 28% → 6% clamped.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Justifies v10's interface economics: 16 KV slots per layer is not too narrow — the paper's workspace carries <10% of variance and tens of concepts. And it warns that a high-variance-explaining probe on thought_states can be entirely off-channel; the audit must intervene on exactly the coordinates the reader consumes (the slot inputs), which our engineered interface lets us do exactly, with no pseudoinverse approximation (§2.5 patching machinery is unnecessary here — we own the tensors).

findings.claim: Small-number/digit content is the weakest-loading workspace category and swaps poorly — a direct caution for HLWM's digit-arithmetic anchors.
findings.paper_evidence: §3.4: 'number-word arguments have the lowest loading and swap poorly'; the paper flags two readings — computation over small integers happens outside the workspace, or integer representations don't align with token lens vectors (§9.1 vocabulary-restriction limitation).
findings.hlwm_relevance: Our banded anchors (digits 2–6) sit in the paper's worst category for workspace mediation. Mitigations already available: grade flips on the final answer string (not intermediate digits), and rely on the Fig 21 result that counts DO enter the workspace when needed for a downstream operation. But preregister the expectation that digit-family flip rates may lag any symbolic/categorical family, so a family-stratified flip readout is required, not a pooled one.

lenses.concrete_proposal:
Three new audit arms + preflights, all audit-only (no new trainable params, no new losses, no gates on zero-init anything), as a prereg amendment section (§12) to reports/hlwm-v10-plan-2026-09-03.md.

ARM (i) GOLD-INJECTION ("reader liveness"; paper §3.1 Fig 7/8 injection): in /Users/karthik/Documents/ChatGPT/Light of the Embel/artifacts/kaggle/hlwm-v10.0/bundle/hlwm_kaggle/evaluate_v10.py add `arm_gold_injection(model, prepared, *, max_new_tokens=48)`: for each masked, non-abstention core row, `oracle = compressed_gold_thoughts(model, trace_ids, trace_mask, model.config.latent_thoughts)` (import the exact function from train_kaggle.py — it is the same tensor Group C trains the consumer on every odd step), then `_decode_v10_row(model, item, oracle, oracle, use_prefix_slots=True, route_index=item.route_index)` — passing oracle as BOTH embeds and states, byte-matching Group C's call `student_channel_teacher_force(..., colar_thoughts, colar_thoughts, ...)`. Touch-point: `prepare_rows` (line ~309) gains `trace_ids/trace_mask` on PreparedRow, encoded from the row's `v10` payload via the shared `encode_trace_segments` (data.py line 745); abstention rows are excluded (trace lib raises by design). GATES (paired_lower_confidence_bound machinery, identical rows): `gold_injection_beats_floor` (LCB>0 ⇒ reader alive) and diagnostic contrast `gold_injection_minus_full` (LCB>0 ⇒ writer is the bottleneck; ≈0 with both high ⇒ channel healthy; both at floor ⇒ interface dead — preregistered 3-way interpretation table, each cell naming which component the next rung repairs). Cost: +1 greedy decode per masked core row (~215 rows ≈ 7–12 min).

ARM (ii) DONOR-KEY FLIP REGRADE ("content-specific steering"; paper §3.3 Fig 13/15/16, 54–70% flips): zero extra decodes. In the grading section (near `grade_arm`, line ~728), re-grade `arm_shuffled`'s existing decode_ids against each donor row's answer spec (`donor_indices` is already returned). Metric: flip_rate = matches-donor-key / rows-where-donor-answer≠own-answer, with Wilson 95% CI, reported PER FAMILY (digit-family caveat, paper §3.4). Preregistered reading: flip_rate high ⇒ channel transmits row-specific content; flip≈0 while shuffled-accuracy≈full-accuracy ⇒ the family-ID-relay confound is CONFIRMED (currently only assumed falsified by degradation); flip≈0 with shuffled≈floor ⇒ content-necessity without steerability, i.e., the paper's 'present but not consumed as argument' state. First run: descriptive with a pre-declared claim threshold (flip_rate LCB ≥ 0.25 required before any 'content transmission' sentence enters the paper); not a pass/fail rung key.

ARM (iii) DOSE-RESPONSE (paper §3.1 Fig 7 strength sweep; §3.4 alpha=2 doubling 76→101/192): `arm_dose_response` on a seeded 64-row masked subsample; thoughts_lambda = (1−λ)·pause_tensors + λ·real_tensors for λ ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} (endpoints reuse arm_pause/arm_full decodes). Report accuracy(λ) + Spearman monotonicity as telemetry (never a gate — a monotonicity gate is structurally hard at n=64). Cost: 192 decodes ≈ 7 min. Optional companion (paper §3.5.2 targetedness): top-1 agreement between full and slot-ablated next-token predictions over 64 neutral continuation prompts, telemetry only.

BLOCKING CPU PREFLIGHTS (added to v10_preflight in train_kaggle.py + unit tests in test_evaluate_v10.py, tiny config): (P-i) gold-injection parity — on a fixture batch, assert the arm's oracle tensor is torch.equal to Group C's colar_thoughts and that the decode path runs with it; assert every masked core row's v10 payload yields ≥ latent_thoughts trace tokens (else raise pre-launch, not mid-audit). (P-ii) endpoint identity — λ=0 decode ids bit-equal to arm_pause, λ=1 bit-equal to arm_full on the tiny model (catches any interpolation/mode-embedding mismatch: note arm_pause ADDS the MODE_SYNTHESIS embedding while compressed_gold_thoughts does NOT — interpolate in the exact post-construction tensors, and the gold arm must NOT add the mode embedding, matching Group C). (P-iii) flip accounting — seeded derangement deterministic; denominator excludes donor-answer==own-answer pairs; a family whose rows all share one answer contributes zero denominator and is disclosed, never silently counted. Total added audit time < 25 min against the ~3h audit budget; total new code ≈ 150 lines + ~120 lines of tests; one day of work fits.
lenses.what_does_not_transfer: The J-lens instrument itself does not transfer and is not needed: the paper's workspace is discovered inside a frozen model via corpus-averaged Jacobians (1000 pretraining-like prompts, vocab-indexed lens vectors, pseudoinverse coordinate patching); HLWM's workspace is an engineered, owned interface (thought tensors → KV slots), so we import the experimental LOGIC (inject/swap/flip/dose/targetedness) with exact tensor substitution instead of first-order approximations. Layer-band findings (§4.1 intermediate workspace range, motor regime in final layers) don't map — our slots inject at all 28 layers by design. Scale does not transfer: directed modulation strength 'tends to increase with model size' (§3.2), swap success rises Haiku→Sonnet/Opus (54→70%), and on Haiku 4.5 'J-space ablation degrades coherence before yielding any qualitative change' — at 0.6B, zero-shot instruction-driven summoning/holding (§3.2 protocols) and experiential-report scoring (§3.5.3) are out of reach and are deliberately NOT proposed; our summoning analog is probe telemetry, not instruction-following. §5 alignment auditing and §6 persona findings are irrelevant to the channel question. Finally, the paper's positive results are on a model whose workspace emerged from pretraining; ours must be trained into existence in 2000 steps — the paper tells us how to MEASURE a workspace, not that one will form, so all three arms are diagnostics with preregistered negative interpretations rather than promises of a pass.

lenses.lens: LAYER BAND, CAPACITY, AND COUNTERFACTUAL REFLECTION (arXiv:2607.15495 "Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models" applied to HLWM v10 Dense Supervision)

findings.claim: The workspace occupies an intermediate layer band starting about 1/3 of the way through the model (~L38) and ending shortly before the output (~L92), with three functional regions: sensory (early), workspace (middle), motor (late).
findings.paper_evidence: Section 4.1: 'The analyses above all identify a similar range of layers, beginning about a third of the way through (~L38) and ending shortly before the output (~L92), as the region where the J-space carries persistent, abstract content distinct from both the input tokens and the imminent output.' Figure 27 caption: 'We divide the model's layers into three functional regions — sensory (early), workspace (middle), and motor (late).' Sub-ranges used causally elsewhere: early workspace L38-54, late workspace L75-92 (Appendix A.15/Fig 69). Models: Claude Sonnet 4.5 by default, corroborated on Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5/4.6 (Section 2, 'By default, we report results on Claude Sonnet 4.5...').
findings.hlwm_relevance: Depth-fraction transfer to HLWM's 28-layer Qwen3-0.6B: onset at ~1/3 depth = layer 9 (0-indexed, 9.33); L38=1/3 implies total ~114 layers, so end fraction 92/114 ≈ 0.81 = layer ~22.6. Derived band for HLWM: layers 9-22 inclusive (14 of 28 layers); sensory 0-8; motor 23-27. Early-workspace analog: layers 9-13; late-workspace analog: layers 18-22.

findings.claim: Band membership was determined by four converging J-lens statistics plus a lens-free causal check: CKA block structure of J-lens vector geometry across layer pairs, top-k next-token prediction accuracy (jumps in final layers = motor onset), excess kurtosis of readouts (rises ~1/3 through = workspace onset), top-1 token autocorrelation across positions, and effective linear dimensionality; activation patching confirms the same depths causally.
findings.paper_evidence: Section 4.1 and Figure 28 (panels a-d); 'The resulting [CKA] matrix has a clear block structure: an early block encompassing roughly the first third of the model, a long middle block, and a small late block'; 'In § A.24 we confirm this ordering causally—activation patching experiments reveal the same depths identified by the J-lens to be the ones that are causal.' Section 4.1.1: ignition — with ambiguous mixed embeddings, 'Starting around the workspace onset (layer 38), it instead sits near one endpoint or the other, switching sharply' (Figure 29). Caveat in 4.1: 'in some models the transition is more gradual, sometimes containing sub-blocks, and that the observed sharpness is exaggerated by layer subsampling.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: The band is real but its boundaries are model-specific and can be gradual — this argues for a soft prior (gate init bias) over a hard restriction in HLWM, since nobody has measured the band on a 0.6B model. The kurtosis/autocorrelation statistics are cheap and could even be computed for Qwen3-0.6B with a logit lens as a telemetry sanity check, but that is optional.

findings.claim: Outside the band, content is either absent/unusable (early: J-lens readouts noisy and uninterpretable, near-zero kurtosis, vectors collapse to a low-rank subspace; may carry only non-verbalizable parsing features) or output-committed (late: 'motor' representations of the imminent token).
findings.paper_evidence: Section 2.2: 'roughly the first third of the model, the readouts are noisy and largely uninterpretable'; Section 9 ('The role of early layers'): 'the J-space carries little content in roughly the first third of the model's depth... low-level parsing features that § A.18 identifies as existing outside the J-space'; Section 4.1: final layers 'function as motor representations that drive the imminent output.' Appendix A.15/Figure 69: 'The two ablation depths produce opposite effects... Ablating at the late layers simply makes the model less likely to say the concept... Early-layer ablation leaves naming largely intact but raises the avoidance failure rate roughly fivefold' — early-workspace content supports flexible use; late-layer content is the output intention itself.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Injecting 16 K/V slots at motor layers (23-27 in HLWM) perturbs output-token selection directly rather than reasoning — this is precisely the mechanism class behind HLWM's historical scaffold-emission pathology (v6.0: latent prefix read as end-of-turn). Injecting at sensory layers (0-8) puts slots where downstream circuits do not treat residual content as workspace material. Both argue for down-weighting, not zeroing, out-of-band gates.

findings.claim: In-band content is preferentially broadcast: MLP blocks amplify J-space-aligned directions to roughly 10x within the workspace range, with gain near 1 before onset and falling again in final layers; a small set of attention heads broadcasts workspace content across positions.
findings.paper_evidence: Section 4.3.1 and Figure 32: 'their gain sits near 1 before the workspace onset, rises through the workspace range to roughly 10×, and falls again in the final layers. The neuron output directions, by contrast, have gain near 1 throughout.' Section 4.3 header result: 'J-space contents are widely broadcast along both [depth and sequence axes].'
findings.hlwm_relevance: This is the strongest quantitative argument for band-biased gate initialization: slot content injected in-band gets ~10x downstream MLP amplification for free, so the same gate magnitude buys far more functional influence at layers 9-22 than at 0-8 or 23-27. It also predicts the learned gate profile should drift toward the band — a falsifiable telemetry prediction HLWM can log per layer at zero cost.

findings.claim: Capacity: J-space occupancy plateaus at ~25 active J-lens vectors (median, per position, pooled over the band), explains <10% excess activation variance; functionally only ~6 UNRELATED concepts are held at once (best rank over band, top-25 threshold), and only 1-2 at any single layer — effective capacity comes from storing different concepts in different layers. Related concepts load as one category (entire 80-word family present), and a category switch clears old items within a few words.
findings.paper_evidence: Section 4.2/Figure 30: 'Occupancy is near zero through the first third of the layers and rises to a plateau of around 25 (in the median case)'; 'The excess variance explained is modest, never exceeding 10%.' Figure 31: 'When the words are unrelated, only around six of those read so far are present at any given comma'; 'the number of list items simultaneously represented at a single layer is even smaller, around one to two (see Figure 72 in § A.16)'; A.16: 'the J-space's effective capacity is increased by the ability to store different concepts in different layers.' Abstract: 'holds on the order of tens of concepts at a time.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: 16 slots/layer is comfortably sized: above the measured per-single-layer load (1-2 items), on the order of the per-position vector occupancy (~25), and above the ~6-unrelated-concepts functional limit. HLWM's K=6 continuous thoughts coincidentally matches the ~6-concept functional capacity. The distributed-across-layers finding independently vindicates v10's per-layer K/V slot design over the v6-v9 single embedding splice. No slot-count change needed; add per-slot attention-mass telemetry to see how many slots carry load.

findings.claim: Counterfactual reflection training recipe: 10,000 task prompts from production RL environments; partial rollouts generated with the baseline model (Claude Haiku 4.5) truncated at a randomly selected turn; a short reflection question appended (e.g. 'Pause here. Are there principles you should be thinking about that you haven't yet?'); target reflections written by the baseline model with a 20-principle constitution excerpt in scaffold, scaffold stripped from the final training example; fine-tune computing loss ONLY on the reflection turn; at evaluation the model is never prompted to reflect and never emits reflection text.
findings.paper_evidence: Section 7: 'We assemble a set of training contexts by sampling ten thousand task prompts from production RL training environments and generating partial rollouts with the baseline model (Claude Haiku 4.5), truncating each at a randomly selected turn... At the truncation point, we append a reflection question... Critically, the constitution excerpt is included only at generation time... We then fine-tune the baseline model on this corpus, computing loss only on the reflection turn... in our evaluations, we never prompt the model to reflect.' Figures 47-48.
findings.hlwm_relevance: The recipe is mechanically adaptable to HLWM because every v10 row already carries a gold trace: truncation point = random step boundary in the gold trace; reflection question = fixed probe string; target = deterministic serialization of trace state (no LLM generation needed). Loss-on-reflection-turn-only maps directly onto HLWM's existing label-masking machinery in student_channel_teacher_force.

findings.claim: Counterfactual reflection training works and the effect is causally carried by implanted workspace content: fabrication dishonesty drops 0.25 to 0.07 and deception 0.38 to 0.05; after training the J-space at evaluation positions carries ethics/reflection tokens it did not before; ablating the implanted lens vectors (176/63 tokens) at workspace layers reverses the gain (0.07 back to 0.22 on fabrication, exactly base level; 0.05 to 0.23 on deception) while leaving the base model unchanged (0.25 to 0.25).
findings.paper_evidence: Section 7: 'Reflection fine-tuning lowers the dishonesty score from 0.25 to 0.07 on the fabrication benchmark (Figure 49, panel A), and lowers the deception score from 0.38 to 0.05 (Figure 50, panel A)'; 'ablation leaves the base model essentially unchanged (0.25→0.25) but raises the reflection-trained model from 0.07 to 0.22, back to base-model level. The behavioral improvement... is thus almost entirely carried by the ethical-reflection-related lens vectors that training implants.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: This is the paper's only training intervention and it demonstrates the causal direction HLWM needs: supervising VERBALIZATION of internal state (never emitted at eval) installs content in the workspace that silent reasoning then actually uses. It is the exact inverse of HLWM's ten-study failure signature (probe-decodable ~0.30 but generation-inert 0.000): v10's premise probe (modeling_hlwm.py:2265 _premise_probe_loss) is a linear contrastive probe — the very instrument class that certified 'information present' while generation stayed dead. A reflection CE loss supervises the same readout THROUGH THE GENERATION CHANNEL, conditioned on the KV prefix as the only source of withheld premises, so gradient must flow through KVPrefixProjector into a generation-usable format.

findings.claim: The workspace account's core prediction, stated explicitly, is that changing what the model is disposed to SAY if asked to reflect changes how it silently REASONS in that context even when never asked — i.e. verbalizability is not epiphenomenal but the format of flexible computation.
findings.paper_evidence: Section 7 opening: 'changing what the model is disposed to say in a context, if it were asked to reflect on its thinking, should change how it reasons there, even when it is never asked.' Section 3.5.1: the J-space 'mediates explicit report and flexible inference but not automatic processing.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: HLWM's continuous thoughts are trained by distillation/probes to CONTAIN premise information but nothing has ever forced them to be VERBALIZABLE FROM THE GENERATION CHANNEL. Per this paper, non-verbalizable content sits outside the workspace and is unavailable for flexible use — a parsimonious explanation of ten studies of 'content present, generation inert.' Reflection supervision is the cheapest way to impose verbalizability on the slot channel.

lenses.concrete_proposal:
THREE CHANGES, all prereg-amended (new plan section, no silent edits), all with blocking CPU preflights, total wall-clock cost <= ~4% of the 12h session.

(a) BAND-BIASED GATE INITIALIZATION — bias, not restriction. Keep slot injection at all 28 layers and all gates learnable (the paper warns transitions can be gradual and sub-blocked in some models, and the band has never been measured at 0.6B; hard restriction would also break the existing gate-closed-equivalence preflight). Derived band from the paper's depth fractions (onset 1/3 -> layer 9; end 0.81 -> layer 22, 0-indexed): IN-BAND layers 9-22 init tanh(g)=0.12, OUT-OF-BAND layers 0-8 and 23-27 init tanh(g)=0.03. Both strictly inside (0,1) so the existing HLWMConfig validation (modeling_hlwm.py:285-288, 'must lie strictly between 0 and 1') holds unchanged per layer; gates stay post-softmax (RMSNorm cannot silence them) and wd-exempt (train_kaggle.py:3189 pattern 'prefix_attn_gate'), so no zero-init and no structurally dead gradient — the 0.03 gate still passes gradient from step 0. Touch-points: HLWMConfig gains prefix_attn_gate_band:(int,int)=(9,23) and prefix_attn_gate_out_init:float=0.03; the attention-module constructor (modeling_hlwm.py:428-444) takes layer_index and selects atanh(init) accordingly; extend the existing per-layer gate-median telemetry (train_kaggle.py:3486) and gate-grad liveness sum (train_kaggle.py:3988) to report in-band vs out-of-band aggregates — falsifiable prediction logged descriptively: learned gates should grow in-band (10x MLP gain region) and shrink at motor layers. Preflight P-BAND (CPU): construct model, assert per-layer tanh(gate) equals the configured profile, run one synthetic backward, assert every layer's gate grad is nonzero and gate-closed equivalence still exact. Compute cost: zero.

(b) SLOT COUNT — NO CHANGE, ADD TELEMETRY. 16 slots/layer fits the paper's numbers (per-layer measured load 1-2 items, per-position occupancy ~25 vectors, ~6 unrelated concepts functionally); K=6 thoughts matches the ~6-concept functional capacity; the paper's capacity-is-distributed-across-layers result (A.16) is direct support for the per-layer K/V design. Add per-layer mean attention mass per slot to telemetry so the audit can report effective slot usage. Cost: zero.

(c) MECHANICAL COUNTERFACTUAL REFLECTION LOSS (the important one — targets the ten-study failure signature directly). Data: in the trace library, add build_reflection_variant(row, rng): truncate the gold trace at a uniformly random step boundary k in [1, n-1]; append a FIXED probe turn ('Pause. Before continuing: state what has been established so far and what remains to be determined.'); target = deterministic serialization of trace state at step k (premises consumed with values, intermediates computed, remaining goal), rendered from the structured gold trace — no LLM generation, fully reproducible, built at bundle time. Loss: standard student-channel CE computed ONLY on the reflection-turn tokens (reuse the existing label-masking path in student_channel_teacher_force), conditioned on the MASKED prompt + KV-prefix slots + truncated trace, so on masked rows the slots are the only source of the withheld premise content — the CE gradient therefore forces KVPrefixProjector to encode premises in a generation-readable format (mirrors Section 7's loss-only-on-reflection-turn discipline; scaffold-free targets mirror their stripped constitution). Schedule: substitute (not add) the student-CE objective on every 4th micro-batch within the accum-16 step, weight --reflection-ce-weight 0.25; substitution keeps wall-clock ~unchanged (same forward shape); if run additively instead, +1 forward on 25% of micro-batches ~ +4% of 6.5h train. Keep the existing premise probe (w=0.1) as the CONTRAST instrument: probe-acc high + reflection-CE low would reproduce the failure signature and is now measurable DURING training. Preflights (CPU, blocking, added to v10_preflight): P-REFL-1 builder determinism (two builds byte-identical) and truncation-boundary validity; P-REFL-2 leak check — on masked rows, assert withheld premise token ids appear in reflection LABELS but never in reflection INPUT ids (info asymmetry preserved; the target may verbalize premises precisely because only the latents carry them); P-REFL-3 gradient liveness — one reflection-CE backward yields nonzero grads on KVPrefixProjector.up, .down, slot_queries, and every prefix_attn_gate; P-REFL-4 schedule test — over 16 synthetic micro-batches exactly 4 are reflection-substituted. Audit: add a DESCRIPTIVE arm to evaluate_v10.py, reflection_readout_f1 — interrupt held-out masked rows with the probe, decode the reflection, token-F1 of withheld premise content against gold; this is the generation-channel counterpart of the probe metric and is explicitly non-confirmatory this study (no new gates; prereg amendment states it may be promoted to a gate in v11 if v10 passes rung 2). Tests: ~10 new CPU tests on the 140-green suite (builder, leak, band init, liveness, schedule, config validation, gate-closed equivalence regression). Total added session cost: <=15-25 min of 12h.
lenses.what_does_not_transfer: (1) The band coordinates themselves: measured on Claude Sonnet/Haiku/Opus 4.5 — frontier-scale, heavily post-trained models with ~114 layers; the 1/3-to-0.81 depth fractions are an extrapolation to a 28-layer 0.6B base+LoRA model, and Section 6 shows post-training itself reshapes workspace contents, so a lightly-tuned small model may have a weaker, shifted, or more gradual band (the paper itself flags gradual/sub-blocked transitions in some models) — hence init bias, never hard restriction. (2) The J-lens instrument: corpus-averaged per-layer Jacobians to the final layer are not being built here; all band claims enter HLWM only as priors plus cheap telemetry, not as a measurement we replicate. (3) The capacity numbers count J-lens vectors active in the RESIDUAL STREAM at a token position; HLWM slots live in attention K/V space and never enter the residual stream directly — 'slots vs tens of concepts' is an analogy of order-of-magnitude, not a validated mapping. (4) Their reflection targets are model-written, constitution-grounded normative prose distilling a DISPOSITION; ours are mechanical state serializations testing latent READOUT — we inherit the training principle (supervise only the counterfactual verbalization, loss on the reflection turn only) but not the alignment result, and their honesty-benchmark effect sizes (0.25->0.07 etc.) carry no quantitative prediction for premise-readout F1. (5) Their training was a dedicated fine-tune on 10k reflections on a frontier model; HLWM gets a 0.25-weight objective on 25% of micro-batches inside a 2000-step multi-loss LoRA run — the causal-implant result may simply be underpowered at this budget, which is why reflection metrics stay descriptive this study. (6) Ignition (4.1.1) and broadcast-head results are diagnostic phenomena with no direct architectural lever for HLWM beyond the gate-init prior already taken.

lenses.lens: DECLARATIVE ATTENTION MECHANICS AND THE TRAINED-DA VARIANT (arXiv:2609.02737 deep-read → trained-DA design for HLWM v10 at 0.6B)

findings.claim: The DA protocol is exactly three modes with a permanently-attended scaffold, and the mask is derived from generated text by a trivial state machine — the whole mechanism is a per-step boolean key-visibility vector, which our SDPA-mask codebase can enforce natively with no kernel work.
findings.paper_evidence: §2: '<global> attends to all context segments... <focus> attends only to the context segments named in the tag... <local> attends to none of the context segments'; §2.3 'Parsing and mode transitions': 'The DA state machine starts in the default global mode... transitions on the closing ">" character of an opening tag (<focus magic_chunks="K"> or <local>) and reverts to global on the matching closing tag. The <global> tag is prompting structure only.' Appendix B 'Always-attended regions': three regions stay attended in every mode — a 16-token attention sink on a fixed system instruction, the question+instruction window, and 'the entire response generated so far.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: Our HLWMAttention.forward already builds an explicit boolean `allowed` mask and ANDs `key_valid` into it (modeling_hlwm.py:522-527). A per-row [batch,1,L,L] `allowed_override` AND-ed at that line, threaded through HLWMBlock/HLWMBackbone/student_channel_teacher_force, is the entire training-time integration; no analogue of the paper's vLLM block-table hooks is needed because we run full-materialized SDPA on 256-token contexts.

findings.claim: Zero-shot DA is infeasible at 0.6B — protocol adherence, not reasoning, is the collapse mode at small scale — but the paper and its closest prior (SSAS) both say training removes exactly that bottleneck, and in our setting teacher-forcing plus constrained tag decoding makes adherence 100% by construction.
findings.paper_evidence: §6.2: 'Focus success rate rises with model size... from 58% at Gemma-4-E4B to 99% at Gemma-4-31B'; §5.2: Gemma-4-E4B 'retains only 29% of vanilla accuracy, much of which is an outright failure to emit a parseable answer under the protocol.' §1/A.5 on Jin et al. 2024 (SSAS): 'a prior work demonstrates that this behavior can be trained into a model, fine-tuning separately per task on hand-designed context partitions and annotation syntax, within 2K-token contexts... on 7B models.' §8.2: 'significant headroom expected if models are post-trained for the protocol itself.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: Trained-DA for HLWM must be SSAS-shaped (task-specific, hand-designed partition, trained annotation syntax), not the paper's zero-shot protocol. Since we teacher-force declarations from gold traces and can constrain decode to the tag grammar, the paper's dominant small-model failure (unparseable declarations) is engineered out — the residual question is only whether 0.6B can answer under the enforced information restriction, which is exactly the falsifiable claim.

findings.claim: Declarations are mechanically derivable from our gold traces with zero ambiguity: each <<a op b = c>> step is <focus seg=premise> iff an operand is a premise literal, else <local>; the final answer-producing step maps to the paper's mandated closing <local> commitment block.
findings.paper_evidence: Appendix F DA Instruction Prompt: focus is for 'pulling a verbatim value out of magic chunk K' with 'VALUE is the answer the magic chunk provides: a name, number, date...'; local is for 'reasoning that builds on facts you have already extracted via earlier <focus> blocks'; soft requirement 2: 'End with a <local> block that names the single value... you will put inside <answer>. This is the commitment step.' Soft requirement 3: 'Don't try to recall magic chunk content in <local>... Anything you "remember" about a magic chunk you didn't focus on is a guess.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: Our rows already carry premise literals and indexed per-step value literals (data.py _premise_supervision; plan §5 'premise literals + masked-prompt variant... indexed per-step value literals'), so the builder can label every trace step focus/local deterministically and assert the labeling (operands of local steps must be prior-step results). The paper's 'recall in local is a guess' rule becomes a hard guarantee under enforcement: recall is physically impossible, so a hallucinated operand in a local step is graded wrong rather than silently leaked — the collapse-proof property we want.

findings.claim: The grammar for 1-3-step arithmetic should be two enforced modes plus answer — <focus>/<local>/<answer> with a single premise segment — because our prompt has exactly one maskable evidence region; <global> adds nothing and the paper itself treats it as prompting structure, not a mask state.
findings.paper_evidence: §2.3: 'The <global> tag is prompting structure only: global is already the default state between declared spans, so it produces no transition.' §2.1: prompt = always-attended scaffold (system/question/instruction) + context whose 'visibility the DA state machine controls.' Appendix F: focus syntax '<focus magic_chunks="K">VALUE</focus>' with multi-chunk variants.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Our public prompt (data.py:109) has four fixed sections; only '### Instruction' (the premise-bearing user_request) is evidence — declare it segment 1 and keep '### Relevant context/Constraints/Response requirements' + response cue as always-attended scaffold, mirroring Appendix B's three regions. Grammar: trace := (F-step | L-step)+ then answer, F-step := '@F <<a op b = c>>', L-step := '@L <<c op d = e>>', using two reserved single-token markers instead of the paper's XML tags to keep traces inside the never-truncated 96-token budget (current traces ≤30 tokens; XML tags would cost ~4-8 tokens per step, markers cost 2).

findings.claim: DA masking on the teacher pass costs ZERO additional GPU time — it is the same forward with a different precomputed boolean attn_mask — which is the only incorporation shape that fits the already-committed 12h ledger without touching the 1,600-step budget.
findings.paper_evidence: §2.3 'Block-aligned mask construction' and Appendix B: the entire mechanism is mask construction ('an ordinary block list, so existing kernels such as FlashAttention run unchanged'); the model computation is untouched, only which keys are read changes. §5.1: 'The chunked prompt format by itself is nearly lossless: DA-nm matches vanilla accuracy on Gemma (87.01% vs 87.01%).'
findings.hlwm_relevance: In train_kaggle.py:3374-3404 Group A teacher-forces [prompt][gold trace][cue][answer] under plain causal attention. Enforcing per-step declarations there (local-typed trace tokens and all answer tokens lose visibility of the premise span) reuses the identical pass; the mask is built on CPU in V10AnchorCollator from token offsets that encode_trace_segments (data.py:745) already makes exact by construction ('no BPE merge can ever straddle two steps'). Measured v10 step time 13-17s is unchanged.

findings.claim: The composition with our masked-premise necessity instrument is DIFFERENT, not additive: DA substitutes for the masked prompt rather than stacking on it. A model cannot 'declare focus on a premise it cannot see' — focusing on [withheld] markers extracts nothing — so the two instruments are mutually exclusive per row.
findings.paper_evidence: §2/Appendix F: focus mode's function is verbatim extraction from a VISIBLE segment ('you're pulling a verbatim value out of magic chunk K'); D.4 failure category 1 ('Evidence destroyed by segmentation... Accuracy collapses (−30/−21pp) even as per-step attention drops') shows what happens when focus lands on a segment that no longer carries the evidence.
findings.hlwm_relevance: In v10-latent, the student prompt physically lacks the premise and latents summon it. In trained-DA, the prompt CONTAINS the premise but the enforced mask withholds it from local/answer steps, so the only premise→answer path is the declared focus-extraction text. Necessity is then tested by corrupting/shuffling the focus-block content at audit (the text analog of the shuffled-prefix control), not by masking the prompt. Running both simultaneously on one row reproduces D.4 category 1 by construction and would be a preregistered confound, not a stronger instrument. This must be stated in the amendment to prevent an accidental 'stacked' design.

findings.claim: At our 256-token contexts the paper's entire efficiency case evaporates: DA pays off only where the global-attention KV read dominates decode wall-time, which requires long contexts and large-batch serving. The sole surviving motive at 0.6B/256 tokens is the auditable, collapse-proof text workspace.
findings.paper_evidence: §3: 'DA trades more decode steps for lower per-step attention cost, and we expect the savings to outweigh the added steps in large-batch deployments'; §5.4/Table 3: the saving 'comes entirely from the global-memory read... 73% of decode time on Gemma and 86% on Qwen' at contexts up to 244K; §5.3: absolute saving is '−1M at short context' growing to '−21M in the longest bin' — i.e., proportional to raw context length. §8.4 states the non-efficiency motive: 'the tokens that make it auditable are the same tokens that drive the KV reads, a property that serves oversight as much as efficiency.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: At 256-token prompts + ≤96-token traces on a dense 0.6B, the KV read is a negligible share of step time (FFN/projection dominated), so any 'efficiency' framing in our paper would be dishonest. The honest motive is §8.4's: a workspace whose content IS its trained tokens cannot exhibit the ten-study signature (probe-decodable ~0.30 / generation 0.000), because there is no probe/generation gap for text — CE-trained tokens are simultaneously the report and the computation input, and the enforced mask makes their consumption causally verifiable.

findings.claim: The paper's own arm decomposition (Vanilla / DA-nm / DA) is the falsification template trained-DA needs: DA-nm isolates format cost from mask cost, and on our task the DA-vs-DA-nm delta is precisely the 'does enforced information restriction break a 0.6B' question.
findings.paper_evidence: §4 Baselines: 'DA-no-mask (DA-nm): uses the full DA prompt template but with full causal attention. The gap between DA-nm and DA isolates the effect of custom attention masking.' §5.1: 'The mask is therefore the source of both DA's efficiency and most of its accuracy cost... (−1.27pp on Gemma, −2.06pp on Qwen), since the chunked format alone is nearly free.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: Audit arms for the trained-DA arm: (1) DA-enforced (mask on at decode, state machine live); (2) DA-nm (same declared-trace training format, full attention at decode) — isolates whether tags/format alone help or hurt; (3) corrupted-focus (clean mask, focus-block VALUES replaced within family) — the necessity control; plus the existing no-prefix floor. Gates: da_necessity = arm1 − arm3 ≥ 0.10 on numeric masked-equivalent stratum; da_mask_cost = arm2 − arm1 reported (paper predicts small if the decomposition fits the task, and our 1-3-step traces avoid both D.4 failure categories: no global counts, output length independent of context).

findings.claim: Two blocking CPU preflights make trained-DA meet the 'no structurally dead mechanism' bar: an all-global-override bit-equivalence test (mask machinery provably inert when open) and a build-time zero-leak sweep over every row's constructed mask (local-typed positions provably blind to premise keys).
findings.paper_evidence: §2.3: mask construction 'rounding the kept token spans outward to block boundaries so that no token the model declared is ever dropped' — the paper's own correctness invariant is span-exact keep-set construction; Appendix F segmenter: 'the segments form an exact, lossless partition of the context: concatenating them reproduces the input' — exactness of the partition is load-bearing.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Preflight 1 (analog of our gate-closed-equivalence test): collator emits allowed_override with every declaration set to focus-on-everything; forward must equal the plain causal forward bit-exactly, proving the override path adds nothing when open. Preflight 2 (analog of the v9 752-row leak-clean check under the real tokenizer): for all rows, assert every local-typed trace token and every answer token has zero visibility onto premise-span key columns, AND that focus-typed tokens do see them (a mask that accidentally blinds focus steps would silently reproduce the D.4 category-1 collapse). Both run in the 69-test-style CPU suite; both are decidable and gradient-free, so nothing about this mechanism can be 'structurally dead' — enforcement is exact or the build fails.

findings.claim: Full trained-DA as the PRIMARY channel is not justified pre-launch: it answers a different scientific question (text workspace) than v10's committed claim (dense latent supervision), and the plan already preregisters it as the rung-triggered fallback HLWM-2-DA. What IS justified pre-launch is the zero-GPU-cost substrate: builder-derived declarations on every row, the mask-override code path, both preflights, and an optional alternating DA-enforced teacher variant with an auto-disable gate.
findings.paper_evidence: §8.2: 'The remaining limitations are properties of this zero-shot elicitation rather than of the masking mechanism... SFT or RLVR on these task shapes... should teach both the decomposition and the mode-selection policy' — i.e., trained-DA is the paper's own named future work, unmeasured. D.4 'Closing the gap' prescribes SFT for the decomposition. No trained-DA numbers exist anywhere in the paper.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Plan §11.B already names 'HLWM-2-DA (post-v10, if latent channels remain dead at this scale)'. Swapping it to primary would abandon the CODI-distillation claim the whole v10 build serves, violate 'necessity by construction' sequencing (rung 1 is terminal for the GENERATIVE latent mechanism — DA is its designated successor), and add an untested decode-time state machine to a launch-ready 140-green bundle. The correct pre-launch incorporation: ship declarations + masks + preflights so the fallback is one config flag away and the crashed-session salvage pattern (Sessions G/H) can pivot mid-quota without a rebuild; optionally enforce DA on 50% of teacher rows (alternating, like the masked-batch pattern) with gate 'DA-enforced teacher_trace_ce − plain teacher_trace_ce < 0.2 nats at step 600, else auto-disable and disclose' so the distillation targets acquire extract-then-compute structure at zero step-time cost and bounded risk.

findings.claim: Decode-time enforcement needs one HLWM-specific deviation from the paper: our tag markers must be single reserved tokens with transitions applied at the NEXT step's key-visibility vector, because our generate loop is a plain cache-free/KV-cache python loop, not a vLLM metadata-builder hook.
findings.paper_evidence: §2.3: 'It watches for tag transitions in the model's output and updates the attention mask at each decode step'; Appendix B 'Per-kernel patches': 'the DA state machine writes the mask into the request's KV-cache block table at every decode step... requiring no changes to the kernel internals.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: In modeling_hlwm.py's generate (~line 1593 onward) the running attention_mask is already threaded per step; enforcement = maintain a per-row premise_visible bool flipped when the last emitted token is the @L (clear) or @F (set) marker, and zero the premise-span columns of the mask passed to the next forward when clear. Single-token markers make the paper's 'closing > character' parsing unnecessary and un-splittable by BPE. Constrained decoding over {@F, @L, answer-start} at step boundaries (we own the sampler) guarantees the protocol adherence that cost Gemma-4-E4B 42% of its focus calls.

findings.claim: The paper's judge/metric apparatus does not transfer, but its headline metric decomposition does: report per-step attended-token ratio as telemetry only (it is the honest 'mechanism is active' witness), never as a benefit claim.
findings.paper_evidence: §5.2: 'The per-step attention ratio is therefore the cleaner measure of the masking mechanism, while the total reflects the elicitation'; §6.1: '<focus> and <local> attend to only a small fraction of the tokens a vanilla step attends (about 12% and 6% on average).'
findings.hlwm_relevance: For our DA arm, log mean per-step attended fraction during audit decode (expected ~0.5-0.8 at 256-token prompts — far from the paper's 0.06-0.12 because our scaffold dominates). It is a liveness witness: a DA arm whose attended fraction is 1.0 means the state machine never fired (the enforcement analog of the v8 gate-flat-at-0.050 pathology, caught in-session instead of post-hoc). Gate: da_mask_active = attended fraction < 0.95 on rows with ≥1 local step; purely decidable from logged masks.

lenses.concrete_proposal:
PRE-LAUNCH INCORPORATION (amendment §12-DA to reports/hlwm-v10-plan-2026-09-03.md; ~1 day; zero GPU step-time cost on the critical path):

1. BUILDER (scripts side + data.py): for every v10 row, derive `da_modes: List[Literal["F","L"]]` per trace step — "F" iff any operand of the `<<a op b = c>>` step matches a premise literal, "L" iff all operands are prior-step results; assert exhaustiveness (mixed → "F"; unmatched operand → build error). Store in the `v10` payload next to `steps`. Also emit `premise_span_char_offsets` for the '### Instruction' section of build_public_prompt so the collator can find the premise segment after tokenization. Cost: CPU-only, deterministic.

2. COLLATOR (data.py, V10AnchorCollator): new method `_da_allowed_override(...) -> Bool[batch, L_total, L_total]` built from (a) premise-span token columns located via encode_preserving_ends offsets, (b) per-trace-token mode labels expanded from da_modes through encode_trace_segments' exact step/token boundaries (no BPE straddle, already guaranteed), (c) always-attended scaffold = everything except the premise span (mirrors paper Appendix B's three regions). Rows: focus-typed trace tokens keep premise columns; local-typed trace tokens and ALL answer/cue tokens drop them. Emitted as `da_allowed_override` only when the DA arm is enabled in config.

3. MODELING (modeling_hlwm.py): add optional `allowed_override: Optional[Tensor]` kwarg threaded HLWMForConditionalGeneration.student_channel_teacher_force → backbone → HLWMBlock → HLWMAttention.forward; single functional line `allowed = allowed & allowed_override.view(batch,1,L,total)` immediately after line 527's `allowed = allowed & key_valid`. Decode path: per-row `premise_visible` state flipped by two reserved single-token markers @F/@L (added to trace text by the builder for the DA-text fallback format; markers verified single-token under the pinned Qwen tokenizer at build time), zeroing premise columns of the running attention_mask contribution via the same override. Constrained sampling over marker tokens at step boundaries.

4. TRAINING (train_kaggle.py, config-gated, default ON at 50%): alternating-row DA-ENFORCED TEACHER — Group A (line 3378) receives da_allowed_override on even rows, so distillation targets (pre_answer_layer_states) are produced under extract-then-compute information structure. Same FLOPs, same 13-17s step. Telemetry: teacher_trace_ce split by enforced/plain. Decidable auto-disable gate: if (enforced − plain) teacher_trace_ce > 0.2 nats at the step-600 checkpoint, set the flag off for the rest of the run and disclose (no human in the loop; mirrors the trajectory-kill-gate pattern).

5. BLOCKING CPU PREFLIGHTS (test suite + v10_preflight): (P-DA1) all-open override forward is bit-identical to no-override forward (analog of gate-closed equivalence); (P-DA2) build-time sweep over ALL rows under the real tokenizer: every local-typed trace token and answer token has zero premise-column visibility AND every focus-typed token has full premise visibility (a mask that blinds focus steps reproduces the paper's D.4 category-1 collapse); (P-DA3) marker tokens encode to exactly one id each and never appear inside equation text.

6. AUDIT (evaluate_v10.py) — fallback arms shipped but OFF on the critical path, activated only by the preregistered branch: DA-enforced decode arm, DA-nm arm (same trace format, full attention — the paper's §4 ablation), corrupted-focus-content arm (necessity control; within-family value swap). Gates for the fallback run: da_necessity = DA − corrupted-focus ≥ 0.10 (numeric stratum); da_mask_active = mean attended fraction < 0.95 on rows with ≥1 local step; da_mask_cost = DA-nm − DA reported, not gated. COMPOSITION RULE stated in the amendment: the DA instrument REPLACES the masked-prompt instrument per row (mutually exclusive — focus on a [withheld] span is vacuous and reproduces D.4 category 1); the DA arm therefore runs on FULL prompts with enforcement as the necessity mechanism.

7. PREREG LADDER WIRING: HLWM-2-DA (already named in plan §11.B) is promoted from prose to the executable rung-1/rung-2 branch: if the latent channel dies again, the SAME session can pivot to trained-DA warm-start (traces with markers already in the data, masks already in the collator) rather than requiring a rebuild — the Sessions G/H salvage lesson.

BUDGET: items 1-3, 5 are CPU/build-time; item 4 is zero marginal GPU cost with a bounded-risk auto-disable; item 6 adds arms only on the fallback branch (each DA audit arm ≈ the existing per-arm cost, ~0.3h/160 rows, affordable inside the 3h audit envelope only if another descriptive arm is dropped — preregister the swap, corrupted-focus replaces the descriptive memory-only slice). Nothing moves the 1,600-step/12h envelope.
lenses.what_does_not_transfer: (1) The efficiency motive, entirely: the paper's payoff analysis (§3, §5.4, Table 3) is a roofline argument about memory-bound global-attention KV reads at 100K-1M-token contexts on B200-class serving — 73-86% of decode wall-time there, ~nil at our 256-token prompts on a dense 0.6B where FFN/projection GEMMs dominate; any token-savings claim in our setting would be theater. (2) The vLLM machinery: block-table rewriting, block alignment (16-32-token blocks), attention-sink placement, per-kernel hooks (§2.3, Appendix B) — we materialize full boolean SDPA masks, so enforcement is one AND, and 'block alignment' is meaningless at our lengths.
