(3) The magic-chunk delivery apparatus (Appendix F simulated get_magic_chunk tool transcripts, the 2048-token semantic segmenter) — our context is four fixed prompt sections with one evidence segment; segmentation is trivial and no tool-transcript framing is needed. (4) The zero-shot elicitation results themselves: all accuracy/savings numbers (Table 2), the scale trend (§5.2), and the adherence curve (§6.2) measure PROMPTED protocol-following at 4B-31B; they neither predict nor bound trained-forced behavior at 0.6B — the closest measured precedent is SSAS (7B, trained, 2K contexts), still 10x our scale, which is why trained-DA must carry its own necessity gate rather than inherit the paper's deltas. (5) The failure taxonomy is mostly moot but one item transfers as a design constraint, not a result: D.4 category 1 (evidence destroyed by segmentation / focus on an evidence-free segment) is exactly what naive stacking of DA on our masked-premise prompts would manufacture, hence the composition rule. (6) The LLM-judge evaluation stack (rubric generation, Gemini/Qwen judges) — our graders are exact-match/programmatic and stay that way.

lenses.lens: CODE-LEVEL FIT: exact touch-points, tests, risk classes, hours, and build order for integrating arXiv:2609.02737 (Declarative Attention) and arXiv:2607.15495 (J-space global workspace) into the built v10.0 bundle before launch

findings.claim: (d-i, do first) The prereg's own gate-liveness telemetry is NOT in the shipped code: plan §A3 requires 'per-layer tanh(g) and prefix attention-mass telemetry every 100 steps; liveness floors at steps 600 and 1,200 (median prefix attention mass >= 0.02 on layers 8-28) folded into the go/no-go', but train_kaggle.py:3486-3493 logs only a single scalar prefix_gate_median (median over layer-medians) and the go/no-go at train_kaggle.py:3845-3858 checks only masked-numeric EM. This is the exact v8 'prereg-vs-code gap' class, and it also blocks prediction P-J1, which the plan claims 'costs nothing; telemetry already collects it' — false at per-layer granularity.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §4.1: 'The analyses above all identify a similar range of layers, beginning about a third of the way through (~L38) and ending shortly before the output (~L92), as the region where the J-space carries persistent, abstract content distinct from both the input tokens and the imminent output.' P-J1 (plan §11A) predicts gates open predominantly in this band — undecidable without per-layer logging.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Touch-points: v10_training_step (train_kaggle.py:3477-3493) — emit metrics['prefix_gate_by_layer'] = [28 floats of per-head-median tanh(g)] plus a prefix-mass ratio r_l = ||gate*prefix_attended||_F/||word_attended||_F gathered by forward hooks on each QwenSelfAttention during the existing telemetry forward (zero modeling-file change); run_v10_training (train_kaggle.py:3845) — fold 'median r_l over layers 8-28 >= 0.02' into the step-600 warm record and step-1200 gonogo; v10_preflight — BLOCK if the init-time ratio already sits < 0.02 (otherwise the floor is unwinnable at tanh(g0)=0.08 by arithmetic, the exact unwinnable-gate class). Tests: test_per_layer_gate_telemetry_length, test_prefix_mass_zero_when_gates_zeroed, test_gonogo_folds_gate_floor, test_preflight_blocks_subfloor_init_ratio. Risks retired: inert-gradient recurrence invisible to step-0 tests (A3's stated purpose); risk introduced: unwinnable-gate (mitigated by the preflight arithmetic check). ~4-5h, zero GPU-budget cost.

findings.claim: (b) Band-biased gate initialization is a 5-line, zero-risk change: initialize tanh(g) higher (0.10) in the intermediate band (layers ~9-25 of 28, i.e. the paper's ~33%-92% depth) and lower (0.04, never zero) at early/final layers, replacing the flat 0.08.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §4.1: workspace band '~L38 ... ~L92' in percent-depth units; §4.2: 'Occupancy is near zero through the first third of the layers and rises to a plateau of around 25 ... across the workspace band'; early layers 'the J-space collapses to a small linear subspace' and final layers are 'motor' representations.
findings.hlwm_relevance: QwenSelfAttention has no layer index (modeling_hlwm.py:407), so do NOT thread one through the constructor: set per-layer inits post-construction in HLWMForConditionalGeneration.__init__ (after backbone build, ~line 1489) via a helper apply_band_gate_init(model, band=(9,25), band_init=0.10, edge_init=0.04) that fills each prefix_attn_gate with atanh(init_l). Config: two new HLWMConfig fields prefix_attn_gate_band (Optional[Tuple[int,int]]) and prefix_attn_gate_edge_init, validated strictly >0 in __post_init__ (extends the existing 0<init<1 check at modeling_hlwm.py:285-288 — the 'no zero-init gates' hard constraint). Checkpoints carry the parameter so resume is unaffected. Tests: test_band_gate_init_values, test_band_gate_edges_nonzero, test_gate_grad_live_every_layer (extends the existing three-part liveness suite to per-layer granularity). Risks: none of the five classes (all inits positive, no new loss, no mask, no buffer). ~2-3h.

findings.claim: (c) The verbalizability probe upgrade directly instruments the ten-study collapse signature: alongside the trained linear probe (evaluate_v10.py:865 train_premise_probe), read latent thought_states through the model's OWN frozen unembedding (lens(h)=softmax(W_U norm(J_l h)); at last-layer states the logit lens J=I is a validated approximation) and report gold-digit rank/EM. Trained-probe-live + lens-EM-zero = 'content present but outside the verbalizable subspace', the paper's exact mechanism for probe-0.30/gen-0.000.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §2.1: 'lens(h_l) = softmax(W_U norm(J_l h_l))' and 'the rows of W_U J_l [are] the Jacobian lens (J-lens) vectors'; §2.4: 'the two lenses agree closely in the model's last several layers', and the logit lens 'capture[s] much of the workspace-like structure identified by the J-lens, though with somewhat lower reliability (particularly in earlier layers)'; §3.1: non-J-space concept components drive verbal report 'on only 5% of trials' vs 59% for J-space components, and under J-clamp the effect 'falls to zero'.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Touch-points: evaluate_v10.py — new verbalizability_readout(model, latents, rows) beside train_premise_probe: scores = model.lm_head(model.backbone.norm(latents)) restricted to the ~40 digit/operator token ids, report top-k rank of gold digits; wire into the existing probe block and emit next to probe_generation_gap as a preregistered DIAGNOSTIC, never a gate (CHANNEL_GATE_KEYS at evaluate_v10.py:115-122 unchanged — avoids the unwinnable-gate class). v10 already applies the matching training pressure (latent_step_head decode CE through frozen lm_head, modeling_hlwm.py:1468-1475), so this readout is the audit-side certificate of that loss. Tests: test_verbalizability_chance_on_random_latents, test_verbalizability_top1_on_planted_embedding (tiny config, tied embeddings), test_readout_never_gates_verdict. Risks: none structural; CPU-cheap at audit. ~3-4h; upgrade from logit-lens to true J_l basis when the B0 artifact lands (see proposal).

findings.claim: (e) Counterfactual-reflection auxiliary loss is the one genuinely new training term worth shipping: train the student channel to verbalize the withheld premise + trace when a learned reflect-cue is appended to the FULL student context ([masked prompt][K thoughts][reflect cue] -> premise/trace CE, answer excluded), never asking at eval. This differs from the existing reconstruct_from_thoughts (modeling_hlwm.py:2575, which drops the prompt) exactly the way the paper's technique differs from plain reconstruction: the reflection is conditioned on the working context, implanting verbalizable content at the positions generation actually reads.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §7: 'We then fine-tune the baseline model on this corpus, computing loss only on the reflection turn ... in our evaluations, we never prompt the model to reflect'; effect: dishonesty '0.25 to 0.07', and causality: ablating the implanted lens vectors 'raises the reflection-trained model from 0.07 to 0.22, back to base-model level' — trained counterfactual verbalization changes silent reasoning in the uninterrupted context.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Touch-points: modeling_hlwm.py — new reflect_cue_embedding = nn.Parameter(randn(width)*0.02) beside recon_cue_embedding (line 1479; satisfies plan A6.7: learned vector, never a resized vocab row); add cue_embeds: Optional[Tensor] parameter to student_channel_teacher_force (line 2472) to override response_cue_ids. train_kaggle.py v10_training_step Group B: on step%4==2 replace the recon slot with reflection CE (targets = trace_input_ids + withheld premise ids, target NEVER includes the answer span — copy-shortcut guard, plan risk 6), weight 0.2, metric 'reflection_ce', own grad_probe group. Scheduling INSIDE the existing recon alternation makes the marginal step cost ~zero against the 13.5-17 s/step wall-clock-bounded ledger (A4) — a naive extra pass would be a budget blowout. Tests: test_reflection_grad_live_isolated, test_reflection_cue_roundtrip_not_vocab_row, test_reflection_targets_exclude_answer, test_recon_reflection_schedule. Risks: budget blowout (mitigated by slot-sharing), gradient conflict (existing cosine telemetry covers it), inert-gradient none (plain CE through the live channel). ~5-7h. Evidence caveat: measured at Haiku-4.5 scale on 10k rollouts; 0.6B transfer is the extrapolated part.

findings.claim: (a) J-space projection of slot values must ship as a SOFT, flag-gated blend (default OFF), not a hard projection: value slots v are blended v <- (1-beta)v + beta*P_l(v) in residual coordinates against a precomputed per-layer task-token J-basis, with beta a config float defaulting 0.0. Hard projection is a silent-mask-death machine (it structurally deletes whatever the projector learned outside the basis), and the prereg already scopes this as contingency v10.1-J, to fire only if rung 2 recurs with the probe-positive/generation-zero shape.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §3.1: 'swapping along the non-J-space components succeeds on only 5% of trials' and under the J-clamp 'the non-J-space component's effect falls to zero' — writing outside J-space is writing where the decoder cannot verbalize; §2.3/§4.2: the J-space carries under 10% of activation variance, so an unconstrained projector lands outside it by default. Plan §11A contingency v10.1-J: 'project slot values into an approximate J-space ... Writing where the decoder verbalizes, by construction.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: Touch-points: HLWMConfig new fields kv_prefix_jspace_blend: float = 0.0 (validated 0<=beta<=1) and jspace_basis_rank; KVPrefixProjector (modeling_hlwm.py:1316-1339) — register_buffer('jspace_basis', zeros(layers, width, r), persistent=True) filled by the bundle loader from a shipped npz; in forward, after the einsum up-projection, map value slots through the frozen per-layer o_proj-composed basis blend on the VALUE tensor only (keys untouched — they set addressing, values set content). CRITICAL resume risk: adding a persistent buffer changes state-dict keys, and the loader is strict=True (plan A6.4) — register the buffer ONLY when the flag is on, and extend the resume test to cover both flag states, else any v10.0 session checkpoint becomes unloadable by v10.1-J (resume-corruption class). Tests: test_blend_zero_is_bitwise_identity, test_projector_grad_live_at_beta_1 (gradient through P is P, live but constrained — assert nonzero), test_basis_orthonormal_per_layer, test_resume_both_flag_states. Risks: silent-mask-death (soft blend + identity-at-zero test), resume corruption (conditional registration), inert-gradient (grad-live test at beta=1). ~4-6h after B0.

findings.claim: (g) A J-space intervention audit arm (arm_jspace_ablation) is a cheap, high-information sibling of arm_steering: project the task-token J-component OUT of thought_states before the projector and decode; paired against the full arm it asks whether the channel's causal content rides in the verbalizable subspace. It must be descriptive (never in CHANNEL_GATE_KEYS) and run on a 64-row sub-core, because a full 160-row arm costs ~0.85h/seed against a ledger with 0.3h total slack.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §2.5 (Writing): ablation is 'projecting out the component of h along v_t entirely'; §3.1 clamp protocol: 'clamping the relevant J-lens coordinates to their clean-pass values ... the non-J-space component's effect falls to zero'; §7 panel C shows the same ablation logic certifying which subspace carries a trained behavior.

lenses.what_does_not_transfer: (1) DA's zero-shot protocol: measured only on 27-31B instruct models, gap widens as scale drops (4B->31B trend read in reverse), and even 27B models fail the protocol inside thinking tags — a 0.6B base cannot follow it, so only the TRAINED variant (Jin et al. 2024 precedent) transfers, and only as the post-v10 fallback. (2) DA's motivation is inference efficiency at 100K-1M-token contexts with vLLM block-aligned KV masking; our prompts are a few hundred tokens, so the 31-52% attended-token savings and the roofline analysis are irrelevant — only the mask-enforcement idea transfers. (3) J-space quantitative anchors (workspace band ~L38-92 percent-depth, occupancy plateau ~25, 6-7% concept variance, tens of concepts) were measured on Sonnet/Haiku/Opus 4.5-class models; a 0.6B may have a shifted, gradual, or absent band — which is why (b) is an init bias not a hard restriction, and P-J1/occupancy are report-only. (4) The J-basis is computed on the pinned frozen base, but LoRA training moves the effective Jacobian — basis drift is undisclosed in the paper's setting (they analyze fixed models) and must be a disclosed limitation for (a)/(g). (5) Counterfactual reflection was validated with 10k RL-environment rollouts on a frontier assistant with chat scaffolding and a constitution corpus; our transfer keeps only the structural core (loss on the counterfactual verbalization turn, never elicited at eval) on synthetic traces — the behavioral-magnitude numbers (0.25->0.07) carry no quantitative expectation at 0.6B/8.8k presentations. (6) Full d x d J_l matrices and 1000-prompt corpus averaging are out of budget; only the ~200 task-token row form transfers.

lenses.lens: ADVERSARIAL SKEPTIC — the case against pre-launch integration of arXiv:2609.02737 (Declarative Attention) and arXiv:2607.15495 (J-space global workspace) into the frozen, 140-tests-green HLWM v10 bundle

findings.claim: P2's workspace claims are measured exclusively on frontier-scale production Claude models; whether a 0.6B model has any coherent J-space is explicitly an open question in their own limitations, with 'none at all' listed as a live possibility.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §2.2: 'By default, we report results on Claude Sonnet 4.5, but we corroborate key results on Haiku 4.5 and Opus 4.5... and in some sections... Opus 4.6' (workspace band cited as layers L38-92, implying ~100 layers). §9.1 'Relationship to model size, architecture, and training dynamics': 'We have studied the workspace primarily in fully trained production LLMs of considerable size... we do not know... how it scales with model size. Future work could investigate whether smaller models have an equally rich workspace, a proportionally smaller one, a less reliable one, or none at all.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: Any pre-launch mechanism that assumes Qwen3-0.6B has a J-space (e.g., grounding the K=6 continuous thoughts in J-lens directions, or a J-space-projection loss) is built on a premise the source paper itself refuses to assert. This is exactly the blind-redesign pattern the ten-study record punishes.

findings.claim: Within P2's own model range the workspace effects already degrade with scale, so extrapolation to 0.6B (>100x smaller than their smallest subject) points sharply downward.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §3.4: 'The Jacobian-lens coordinate swap succeeds in 54% of trials on Haiku 4.5, 70% on Sonnet 4.5, and 70% on Opus 4.5.' §4/A.23 ablation section: 'on Haiku 4.5, J-space ablation produces a similar reduction in experiential language score in these contexts, though of less dramatic magnitude.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: The one causal-intervention number that moves with scale moves the wrong way for us. A J-space-targeting training loss at 0.6B could be structurally weak or dead — violating the hard constraint 'no losses whose gradient can be structurally dead.'

findings.claim: CONCESSION: the task framing 'post-training installs the workspace' misreads P2 — post-training installs the Assistant's POINT OF VIEW in a pre-existing workspace; the J-space is present and load-bearing in the base model before any RLHF. So 'ours is a base model' is not by itself disqualifying; scale is the disqualifier.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §9.1: 'The post-training comparison of §6 shows that the J-space is present and load-bearing in a base model before any RLHF, so the structure is not solely a product of post-training.' §6.1: post-trained model represents Assistant reactions (safely/unsafe on the Tylenol dose) on user tokens while 'in the base model, the readout at the same position is pain, now, and feels' — i.e., base workspace exists but carries local context, not Assistant reactions.
findings.hlwm_relevance: The honest skeptic's case rests on the 0.6B scale unknown and the frontier-scale-base caveat (their base model is Sonnet-scale), not on base-vs-instruct. Do not overclaim the persona argument in the prereg amendment.

findings.claim: P1 exhibits a measured monotonic capability cliff: the smallest model tested (Gemma-4-E4B, ~4B effective) retains only 29% of vanilla accuracy with 58% protocol adherence, and the paper states DA requires a minimum capability its smallest subjects do not meet. Qwen3-0.6B sits ~7x below that failure point.
findings.paper_evidence: P1 §5.2: 'Relative accuracy increases monotonically with model size on both families: from 29% at Gemma-4-E4B to 99% at Gemma-4-31B, and from 64% at Qwen-3.5-4B to 97% at Qwen-3.6-27B... At the low end, Gemma-4-E4B retains only 29% of vanilla accuracy, much of which is an outright failure to emit a parseable answer under the protocol: its focus-parse success rate is only 58%... This suggests that DA's gains depend on a minimum level of base capability that the smallest models do not yet meet.' §6.2: adherence 'the dominant bottleneck only at the smallest scale.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: A declared-attention protocol (model emits mode tags parsed into masks over context segments or KV-prefix slots) at 0.6B would fail at the parse level before any reasoning benefit — reintroducing the 'emission-path corruption' collapse class (v6.0 scaffold emissions) via a new tag vocabulary.

findings.claim: P1's claim that training could rescue small-model DA is explicit future-work speculation with zero measurements at any scale; even frontier models could not follow the protocol inside thinking traces.
findings.paper_evidence: P1 §8.2: 'We believe a similar pipeline could elicit more optimal use of DA' and 'SFT or RLVR on these task shapes, and larger backbones... should teach both the decomposition and the mode-selection policy that zero-shot prompting cannot yet' (Table 10 discussion). §4 Inference settings: 'We disable thinking mode for all models as preliminary experiments showed that they fail to follow the DA protocol within thinking tags.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: 'Post-training fixes it' is exactly the class of unmeasured extrapolation that produced Studies 5-9. There is no paper evidence that ~2000 LoRA steps on a 0.6B base can install a protocol that 27-31B instruct models only follow zero-shot at 97-99% and 4B models follow at 58-89%.

findings.claim: P1's payoff regime is absent from the v10 setting: DA's entire benefit lands on the global-attention KV read in large-batch long-context serving, while it COSTS 15-35% more decode steps — at v10's short synthetic anchors, batch-1 unpadded audit, and a fixed 12h budget, DA is pure cost with nothing to save.
findings.paper_evidence: P1 §3: 'DA's per-step reduction therefore lands on the global-attention KV read, where decode work concentrates... The savings are therefore largest in large-batch, long-context serving.' §5.4: global memory is 73%/86% of vanilla decode time on B200 at contexts up to 244K. §5.1/Fig 2: 'DA and DA-nm both run roughly 15-35% more decode steps than vanilla.' Benchmark contexts: mean 6.4K-121.7K tokens (Table 1).
findings.hlwm_relevance: v10 anchors are hundreds of tokens; evaluate_v10.py decodes 'row-by-row (batch 1, the unpadded audit)'. There is no attention cost to reclaim, so the integration has no measurable payoff even if the protocol worked — the definition of a solution looking for a problem.

findings.claim: P2's genuinely load-bearing contribution to HLWM is the verbalizable-vs-merely-decodable distinction, which names the ten-study failure signature exactly — but its natural form is a post-run diagnostic instrument (the J-lens), not a pre-launch training mechanism.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §1.3: 'The averaging step is key, as it distinguishes representations that are verbalizable—poised to be spoken about, should the occasion arise—from those that merely happen to be verbalized in one particular context'; 'a principled refinement of the logit lens... allowing it to uncover meaningful information in earlier layers.' §9.2: 'the lens readout is cheap to compute (a single matrix multiplication per layer, with the matrix computed once per model).' A.7: 'J-lens beats the logit lens and tuned lens baselines with as few as 10 prompts.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: 'Probe-decodable ~0.30 but generation-inert 0.000' is precisely 'decodable but not verbalizable.' If v10 fails the same way, a Qwen3-0.6B J-lens (28 layers, d_model~1024 — tractable offline) can determine whether latent content ever entered the causal broadcast path, versus sitting in probe-only subspaces. That is a v10.1 diagnostic, and it only matters AFTER the run produces the failure it would explain.

findings.claim: v10's loss stack already implements the papers' actionable prescription: dense teacher-state distillation at the pre-answer token plus per-latent decode CE through the frozen lm_head are directly 'make the latents causally poised to be verbalized' — P2 supplies a measurement of whether that succeeded, not a loss the plan lacks.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §1.3 defines verbalizability as first-order causal effect on future output likelihood through the model's own unembedding ('Reading from the lens replaces all layers downstream of ℓ with the single linear map J_ℓ followed by the model's own unembedding'). The per-latent decode CE through the frozen lm_head is a logit-lens-style verbalizability pressure, which P2 positions as the baseline the J-lens refines.
findings.hlwm_relevance: Adding a J-space loss pre-launch would duplicate pressure the prereg already applies via producer losses, at the cost of an unvalidated offline Jacobian job and a reopened red-team. The correct pre-launch action is zero code change.

findings.claim: P2's selectivity criterion actively predicts that v10's deterministic family routing may make workspace-style broadcast unnecessary — the J-space is bypassed for automatic computation with a fixed downstream consumer — so a workspace-targeting loss could fight the model's legitimate efficient solution.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §9.1 'Which tasks require the J-space?': 'the J-space is engaged when an intermediate must be handed to an arbitrary, context-specified downstream circuit, and is bypassed when the computation is automatic.' §3.5 title: 'The J-space selectively mediates flexible but not automatic cognition.' §4 ablation: GSM8K with explicit CoT 'substantially more robust to ablation.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: v10 routes latents to deterministic per-family MLP experts — the consumer is NOT arbitrary or context-specified. Per P2's own criterion, a healthy v10 could pass all gates with latents that never look workspace-like. Gating or regularizing toward J-space occupancy would penalize success.

findings.claim: The empirical crash record makes any pre-launch code delta the single largest risk to the program: four of the last five sessions were lost or damaged by one-line-scale changes, and the binding red-team process requires days of new preflights and decidable gates per mechanism.
findings.paper_evidence: (Program record, not paper): v6.0 session D crashed on a missing autocast; v8.0 session F crashed in a stale-field debug print; v9.0 session G crashed on a 5-feature-vs-(3,4) combiner guard; v6.0.1 session B crashed on an orphaned @torch.no_grad. v10 red-team: 23 findings, 7 fatal, folded into binding §10 amendments requiring per-mechanism blocking CPU preflights and decidable gates.
findings.hlwm_relevance: The 140-green suite and red-teamed prereg are the program's only accumulated capital. Neither paper identifies a v10 failure mode that either integration would prevent BEFORE the run's own diagnostics exist; both integrations therefore buy zero expected risk reduction while re-adding the exact crash surface that destroyed sessions B, D, F, and G.

findings.claim: P2's one falsifiable prediction about v10 — workspace content concentrates in an intermediate layer band, near-zero in the first third, motor-dominated at the end — is already testable for free from telemetry v10 logs, requiring no architecture change.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §1.3/§4.1: 'coherent content emerges only after an initial band of layers, and abstract concepts give way in the final layers to representations tied more directly to the imminent output'; §4.2: occupancy 'near zero through the first third of the layers and rises to a plateau of around 25... across the workspace band.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: v10 injects 16 K/V slots at ALL 28 layers with per-layer per-head tanh gates, and train_kaggle.py line 3486 already logs per-layer median tanh(gate); line 4017 snapshots gate tensors. If P2's band structure holds at 0.6B, the trained gate profile will show it — the run itself produces the evidence that would justify (or kill) a v10.1 band-restricted injection. All-layer injection is a strict superset, so the current design cannot be wrong in the direction P2 warns about.

findings.claim: P2's counterfactual reflection training is a behavior-shaping technique for honesty/alignment at production scale (10,000 RL-environment prompts, fine-tuning Haiku 4.5) and has no bearing on HLWM's latent-reasoning claims.
findings.paper_evidence: P2 §7: 'sampling ten thousand task prompts from production RL training environments and generating partial rollouts with the baseline model (Claude Haiku 4.5)... fine-tune the baseline model on this corpus, computing loss only on the reflection turn'; evaluated on fabrication/deception honesty benchmarks. §9.2: 'We do not yet know how broadly the technique generalizes.'
findings.hlwm_relevance: Nothing in the v10 claim set (dense latent distillation efficacy, calibrated abstention) is touched by implanting ethical-reflection concepts. This is the clearest solution-without-a-problem of all candidates: HLWM-2 territory at most.

lenses.concrete_proposal: VERDICTS PER CANDIDATE INTEGRATION. (1) P1 declared-attention protocol (zero-shot or trained, over context segments or KV-prefix slots): HLWM-2. Strongest reason: measured monotonic collapse to 29% relative accuracy / 58% parse adherence at 4B — ~7x above our scale — plus a payoff (global-attention KV read savings at 100K+ contexts) that is physically absent from v10's few-hundred-token batch-1 audit; it prevents no known v10 failure mode. (2) P2 J-space grounding loss / J-lens-direction projection for the K=6 continuous thoughts: CONTINGENT-v10.1, gated on TWO preconditions from the v10 run itself: (a) v10 reproduces the signature (aux premise probe > chance AND masked-generation lift ~0) and (b) an offline J-lens existence check on frozen Qwen3-0.6B passes P2's nonrandomness screen (excess kurtosis of readout logits vs random-matrix control, P2 §4.2).
